A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work by the same authors. The complete main texts, figures, algorithms, equations, and Appendices A–E are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: Sections 5.1–5.2 report original GB1 and RNA design-selection experiments, including error and selection rates. The appendices contain predictor assessments and exceedance-based results.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds GB1 results using estimated density ratios and RNA results using an expanded configuration menu.

M1.justification: The main selection procedure in Algorithms 1–2 is retained, but the documented finite-sample routine changes. Algorithm 4 corrects the residual from prediction-minus-label to label-minus-prediction; Algorithm 5 replaces the two-sided betting construction with the positive betting process alone.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate four-site GB1 binding-affinity design and length-50 RNA binder design. The additional experiments vary density estimation and configuration settings within these existing tasks, without adding datasets or task coverage.

E2.justification: The corresponding GB1 and RNA comparisons retain prediction-only, GMMForecasts with q = 0, 0.5, and 1, CalibratedForecasts, and the conformal method reported as selecting nothing. The expanded RNA menu adds configurations of existing generators, not new selection baselines.

E3.justification: v2 adds a GB1 evaluation using estimated categorical densities instead of exact density ratios (Appendix D.1). It also evaluates an RNA menu expanded from 78 to 249 configurations through AdaLead recombination and VAE architecture settings (Appendix E.1). The original evaluation protocols remain.

E4.justification: New Figure 6 directly checks sensitivity to estimating GB1 density ratios, while new Figure 10 examines selection with a larger RNA menu. These are focused robustness extensions. The existing GB1 exceedance analysis is retained as Appendix D.2 and Figure 7.

E5.justification: The finite-sample confidence-bound calculation changes in Algorithms 4–5, including the residual correction and switch to a one-sided betting process. Empirical reporting practices remain unchanged: the original trial counts and median/20th–80th-percentile summaries are retained, and the added plots use the same summaries.

E6.justification: New Figure 6 reports GB1 behavior closely matching the known-density-ratio results. New Figure 10 reports similar RNA error rates but higher selection rates across a broader threshold range with the expanded menu. These are additional results under changed settings; the original comparison curves and findings are retained.

T1.justification: Appendix A replaces the heuristic efficiency discussion with an explicit asymptotic variance comparison against a labeled-only estimator. The finite-sample proof also corrects a coverage equality to an inequality. The principal theorem statements and extensions remain substantively unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract and contributions retain the same problem formulation, prediction-powered multiple-testing solution, guarantees conditional on known density ratios, and empirical effectiveness with estimated ratios. The additional checks support these existing claims.

C2.justification: v2 adds discussion of Bonferroni conservativeness and possible hierarchical or correlation-aware alternatives. It attributes the expanded menu's higher selection rates to stronger available configurations and states the variance condition underlying prediction-powered efficiency more explicitly.

D1.justification: Section 5 adds a code repository link. Appendix D.1 documents categorical maximum-likelihood density estimation with Laplace pseudocounts of 1, and Appendix E.1 specifies the additional recombination and VAE parameter grids. Existing training and MDRE details are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds Bretz et al. (2009) and Dudoit et al. (2003) to discuss structured multiple testing. The broader research positioning remains stable; the Thomas citation's preprint-to-publication update represents the same work.

P1.justification: v2 revises terminology, groups the forecast baselines, reorganizes the proof discussion, and expands result explanations. Examples include naming the population-level metric and changing feedforward/FF terminology to fully connected/FC. The overall section sequence and narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds Figures 6, 8, and 10 for density estimation, menu structure, and menu expansion. Existing figures receive legend, spacing, and caption refinements; Figure 2 changes its illustrated high-temperature distribution from 0.65 to 0.7. Larger typography also reflows the document; old Figures 6–7 survive as Figures 7 and 9.

improvement.justification: v2 corrects the finite-sample residual sign and a proof inequality, adds focused robustness evidence, and documents code access. These improve correctness, support, and reproducibility within the existing scope. The gains remain bounded: estimated-ratio guarantees are still unavailable, and the larger-menu experiment changes configuration quality alongside menu size.
